source.title: Analyzing the Impact of Optimization Techniques on U-Net-Based Building Detection Performance

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer choices and reports held-out test metrics alongside training and validation behavior, bearing on V4's optimizer/generalization comparison with a different task and model.
record.gate_note: The study compares Adam, Nadam, and RMSprop on U-Net building segmentation and reports test-set classification metrics. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolution versus fully connected architecture, batch-size effects, dropout effects, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study compares three adaptive optimizers on U-Net building segmentation. Without SGD or momentum SGD, its results cannot test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD generalization comparison. It tests no other claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors favor Nadam on most test metrics, describe Adam as more stable and fastest to train, and report the fastest inference with RMSprop. They qualify optimizer performance as dependent on data and system characteristics.
record.recipe_differences: Compares three adaptive optimizers on U-Net building segmentation, without the adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons or benchmark settings specified in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice changed test metrics, training stability and duration, and inference speed in this dataset and U-Net setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Among three adaptive optimizers, Nadam achieves the highest test accuracy (0.9189), recall (0.7499), F1 (0.7713), and IoU (0.6278); Adam achieves the highest precision (0.8436).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizer choice affects held-out building-segmentation performance for U-Net on the Massachusetts Buildings Dataset with experimentally selected learning rates and early stopping.

record.peer_reviewed: The International Archives of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences; paper states that the contribution has been peer-reviewed.
record.problems: Only three trainings are reported, one per optimizer, with no repeated seeds or uncertainty estimates. There is no SGD or momentum-SGD comparator, so the results do not directly test the adaptive-versus-SGD generalization claim. The task and dataset differ from the benchmarks in V4.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance performance on held-out random labels.
Test-error changes with width beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD performance under limited tuning; effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and language-model settings.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout; dropout is fixed at 0.2.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Accuracy effects of removing memorized rather than random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The SGD comparisons in the introduction are cited studies, not this study's results. Only one training per optimizer is reported, with no uncertainty estimates; learning rates and stopping epochs differ across optimizers.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Tests Adam, Nadam, and RMSprop only on one U-Net segmentation task and dataset; does not compare SGD, broader tuning, weight decay, optimizer switching, or language benchmarks.
Large versus small batch training and adaptations to batch size.
Dropout intervention and its effect on test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the test-accuracy effect.

rows.subject: U-Net with Adam optimizer
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; training method otherwise not stated
rows.operation_detail: Train U-Net using Adam and evaluate on test images.

conditions.value: Massachusetts Buildings Dataset; 1000 training, 100 validation, and 150 test images after preprocessing to 256×256 pixel areas
initially 100; early stopping at epoch 22; restored weights from epoch 17

rows.measure: Test accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and IoU
rows.value: Accuracy 0.9132; precision 0.8436; recall 0.6437; F1 Score 0.7302; IoU 0.5751
rows.note: No same-setting SGD or momentum SGD comparison; results cannot establish whether adaptive optimization generalizes worse than those methods.
rows.check: Table 2 values are correctly recorded, but Adam's test metrics have no SGD comparator and therefore do not bear on V4.
